searchText: > The motivation section should explain why this needs to be a Standard rather than just a Good Idea since it isn't immediately obvious. A standard is valuable when there is a many-to-many relationship between parties. An example of something that needs a standard is web pages because there are many browsers that come and go over time and there are many web pages on the internet that come and go over time. In order for all web pages to work on all browsers, we need a standard. If you have a one to many relationship or a one to one relationship, then you don't need a standard and instead just have a Good Idea that you can implement. Thoughts on the wording of that? I find myself typing it out a lot, figured I could refine it and save it somewhere. I would like to point broken links at some 404 page rather than a GitHub issue or pull request, any thoughts on what to put in for a placeholder? The goal is to make it obvious and easy to find when these old EIPs are pointing at PRs and Issues that are not EIPs. cc <@!425279588009246720> <@!543900561460822016> to see if you have thoughts on where these broken EIP links should point. Recap of the situation: People have `[EIP-123](...)` where `123` is not a valid EIP. Usually it is just some pull request or GitHub issue that never even made it to draft status. I would *rather* have those link to a 404 page than link to an issue or PR, as it will make it much easier for us to find and clean them up later, and it will be more clear to users that there is a problem (hopefully). There are about 35 instances of this problem across the repository. > Thoughts on the wording of that? I find myself typing it out a lot, figured I could refine it and save it somewhere. <@!301186049323958275> looks good, you had another sentence that somethings are better documented as part of the project / proprietary product. Maybe include that too? Ideally something like this goes into EIP-1 where it describes the idea stage. Even if something starts out as a proprietary doc, if more products adopt it, it may make sense to turn into an eip at that stage. I'd include this clarification too. What we are trying to avoid is serving as a documentation place for random projects, right? I don't know that people are intentionally creating EIPs as a form of documentation or advertising. I think some of them really don't understand that you don't have to standardize everything. I have no idea about their motivation but extending your explanation with those suggestions may help them consider it better. As long as it is put into EIP-1 and you don't need to copy it to every single review > I would like to point broken links at some 404 page rather than a GitHub issue or pull request, any thoughts on what to put in for a placeholder? Which broken links? Wasn't the idea to revert those links to keep their long form (for now)? Or this is a question post this PR? In this PR I feel very bad putting bad links in. I agree with you that I shouldn't be changing text in this PR, but the links are (IMO) bad links to start with and by being explicit about that it makes it easier for us to find them later. I wonder what happens if I just do `[EIP-123]()`? Not sure how I feel about making substantial changes like marking links to issues as invalid in that PR. Why is it bad changing those instances only which are clear, and then following up with a more tedious process? Because the more tedious process will never be done I suspect. I think it can be done step by step via eipv, and by withdrawin/archiving stuff. I would rather see things hard fail, because that is more likely to be fixed by the authors, than if things just work incorrectly. > I think it can be done step by step via eipv, and by withdrawin/archiving stuff. I think you are more optimistic that I am that we'll see the necessary changes to the EIP validation bot and merge bot. There's must be some money left between the cracks of yield farming to bounty this work out You could ask the sushi person, they have 36,000 ETH. Maybe they want to give back? probably they have DAI/USDC/etc. by now The reason stuff never really improved because there were no "outsourceable" tasks, but I think with the automation proposal list it is possible now to get that work done <@!425279588009246720> thanks for the time and work you put into your EIP overhaul proposal. I'm not likely to throw my opinion into the process but I wanted to voice my appreciation for your work on it. Draft The first formally tracked stage of an EIP. This EIP is merged when properly formatted and is still under development. Review The EIP author marks an EIP as ready for and requesting Peer review. Stagnant Any EIP in DRAFT or REVIEW that has been inactive for a period of 6 months or greater is automaticaly moved to theSTANGNANT status. EIP Authors are notified of any automatic change to the status of their EIP Withdrawn The EIP Author(s) decided to withdraw the proposal. Living A special status for EIPs that are designed to be continually updated and not reach a “Final” state. This includes EIP-1 and other registry EIPs. That is from the hackmd document Last call and Final is as is. And I'd sincerely ask you to consider responding properly on https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/issues/2941 (after reading the discussion) instead of just posting this image there. Is there no way to tell apart why something is withdrawn/abandoned? I responded in the thread. Withdrawn and Abandoned were already merged as you suggested. Stagnant is an additon for reasoning I posted in the thread. An EIP editor marking a status as Withdrawn/Abandoned is a political decision. Which we should avoid having editors make political decisions imo. I'm phrasing this based on #2941: And editor can only mark it `status="Withdrawn" reason="no activity"` . Hopefully if someone implements a bot, the bot can do it, but bots wont write themselves (at least not yet). I do not think this is a political step as long it is clearly stated in EIP-1. `status="Withdrawn" reason="by author"` can only be set by the author, again not an editor decision. Thanks <@!187490121698770945> I think the only confusion here was that the actual meticulous description is yet to be done in the PR changing EIP-1, while the graph and description is just on the high level. <@!301186049323958275> this is a sad PR, as predicted: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/2427#issuecomment-690414083 Okay here's the idea how to clear up the README <> EIP-1 <> *frontpage on eips.ethereum.org* mess: - Change EIP-1 so that it consists of clear chapters, one being "Contributing" - Explain all the tech steps (in the readme now) in Contributing - Merge the anchor headings PR: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/2581 - Replace most of what the README and the *frontpage on eips.ethereum.org* with a link to https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPs/eip-1#contributing

excerpts.author: madeof_tin7509
excerpts.content:
Draft
The first formally tracked stage of an EIP. This EIP is merged when properly formatted and is still under development.

Review
The EIP author marks an EIP as ready for and requesting Peer review.

Stagnant
Any EIP in DRAFT or REVIEW that has been inactive for a period of 6 months or greater is automaticaly moved to theSTANGNANT status.

EIP Authors are notified of any automatic change to the status of their EIP

Withdrawn
The EIP Author(s) decided to withdraw the proposal.

Living
A special status for EIPs that are designed to be continually updated and not reach a “Final” state. This includes EIP-1 and other registry EIPs.
